causes.text: Realtor.com described how Hurricane Milton made landfall on Siesta Key just 12 days after Hurricane Helene, turning leftover debris into shrapnel and scattering it across the island.

source_info.title: After Hurricanes Helene and Milton, Florida islanders face months of cleanup

effects.text: Lowe's forecast a slower decline in comparable sales due to hurricane-driven demand, yet its shares fell about 4% as investors remained cautious about big-ticket spending.

source_info.title: Lowe's sees slower sales drop thanks to hurricane demand but stock falls

causal_reasoning_chain.description: Hurricanes Helene and Milton slammed into Florida within 12 days of each other in October 2024, turning debris into dangerous projectiles and leaving extensive property damage. A Realtor.com account described how Hurricane Milton struck Siesta Key on October 9, 2024, scattering debris across the island and forcing residents to undertake continuous cleanup.

The back-to-back storms spurred a wave of emergency repairs and rebuilding, driving demand for home-improvement supplies such as lumber, shingles and generators. Retailers anticipated higher sales in storm-affected regions even as broader DIY demand weakened.

On November 19 2024, Lowe's forecast a smaller drop in annual comparable sales than previously expected because hurricane-related demand provided a tailwind. However, investors focused on persistent weakness in big-ticket DIY spending and the stock fell roughly 4% in early trading.

rationale: Severe hurricanes created sudden repair demand that partly offset broader weakness. Nevertheless, investors worried about costs and lingering demand softness, causing Lowe's stock to drop.
counterfactual_analysis: Without the back-to-back hurricanes, Lowe's might have faced an even steeper sales decline but the stock drop might have been smaller if investors were not concerned about the cost of storm-related operations.

adversarial_confounders.text: Supply-chain disruptions or inflation could have influenced sales and margins during the same period.
adversarial_confounders.impact: These factors might have exacerbated the stock decline independently of hurricane-related demand.

details.commentary: Severe storms temporarily shift bargaining power toward retailers that still have inventory of critical repair goods. Lowe's can capture outsized demand in affected regions, but investors worry that relying on weather-driven spikes is not a durable edge over rivals.

Back-to-back hurricanes reflect a pattern of more frequent severe weather, which raises baseline spending on repairs and resilience. At the same time, these disasters are episodic, so the underlying economic drag on consumers keeps investors cautious about long-run demand.

Storm damage creates a short-term surge in sales that supports quarterly comps and margins. Once rebuild activity fades and tough year-on-year comparisons roll in, the growth boost unwinds and can expose softer core demand.
